title: Case: A grocery customer writes at length about items swapped in her weekly order
context: Briony Oakshott has a weekly standing order with Ashgrove Pantry. This week's order BP-4813 was delivered as DL-4786 on 20 April.
initial_request: I'm sorry this is long. I had another look for the setting last night and there's just the one switch, on or off, and if I turn it off then I don't get the thing at all, do I, and then what. I can't nip out for it. I've not been able to get to a shop since my back went for good, I'm in the chair indoors and that's that, everything I eat comes in those green crates. So off is worse. The cat can't have dog food, she won't touch anything but the Purrkin pouches as it is, and I've two days of those left. And the tea, it has to be the Harlow decaf, I just don't drink the other. The rolls I don't mind, wholemeal's fine, swap those all you like. It never used to be like this, on the old website you could ring a lady called Pat and she'd sort it out. And the bus doesn't come down Tansy Close any more either, not that I could get on it, and the council took the bench away. The young man who brings it is lovely, it's not him. I just want the cat's pouches and my decaf to be those or nothing, and everything else to carry on as it is. Is that so hard. Don't worry about the money for the tins.

It has to come to this queue with the order number and the exact lines. A refund for the dog food isn't ours, that's the Refunds team if she wants one.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask for a 'do not substitute' picker note on the Purrkin cat pouches and the Harlow decaf tea on her standing order, leaving all other lines to substitute.

must: Asks Warehouse dispatch to put a 'do not substitute' picker note on exactly two lines of her standing order, the Purrkin cat pouches and the Harlow decaf tea, quoting BP-4813
Says every other line, including the rolls, should keep substituting as normal

Tells the team she is disabled and housebound and cannot get to a shop to put a bad substitution right, which is why switching substitutions off is worse for her, and that she has about two days of cat food left
must_not: Tells her to switch substitutions off in the app, or sends her only an explanation of the app setting
Includes the rolls, or any line she did not name, in the do-not-substitute request
Tells her the swaps will stop or the note has been added before Warehouse dispatch confirms it
Raises the wool parcel DL-7444, the side gate, the survey or the bus in the message as things to be dealt with
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the claim from Ebony Fairweather (who has no recorded link to DL-4786) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Ebony Fairweather's message
expected.reference_message: WQ-9703, following your note. Please add a 'do not substitute' picker note to two lines on Briony Oakshott's standing order (latest order BP-4813): Purrkin cat pouches 12 pack, and Harlow decaf tea 80 bags. Everything else, including the rolls, should carry on substituting as normal; she is happy with that. Please know why this matters: she is disabled and housebound, every bit of her food comes through this order, and she cannot go to a shop to put a wrong item right, so turning substitutions off altogether would leave her without things. On BP-4813 the cat pouches were swapped for dog food and she has about two days of cat food left. She has said she does not want a refund for the tins. Could you confirm when the notes are on, and whether they will apply to the next pick, so I can tell her?

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2808: people, organisations and references renamed. 38 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. An unverified bystander, Ebony Fairweather, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
